context: Request: general commercial litigation matters (not specialty litigation such as IP, employment or antitrust) where the firm is seeking compensatory damages, with the pleadings that spell out the damages. Rubric: 14 qualifying matters (1005-00005, 1006-00005, 1010-00005, 1012-00006, 1020-00005, 1021-00006, 1022-00005, 1023-00002, 1024-00003, 1033-00006, 1034-00003, 1035-00004, 1044-00006, 1045-00004), a proof pleading for each, plus a precision criterion (1019-00001 is outside the set).

stages.note: Lists all files of eleven matters the reviewer named.

stages.note: declared: Read documents picked from the file listing; reads one sibling matter's counterclaim. A premature stage_start for writing is rejected because the stage is still open. Reviewer said no; flagged exclusions made without opening documents.

runs.failure_point: Its capped file-name search and its one-word scans never surfaced three qualifying matters; it also dropped two matters it had read, cited only the petition of one matter, and added a non-qualifying matter.

first_error.stage: Search file names for request keywords
first_error.why: The fallback file-name search was cut by its own 300-line cap, and the later chunked scans only kept pleading-named files containing the word 'compensatory', so three qualifying matters never appeared in any result.
first_error.critic_note: Review [23] flagged the line cap and the un-chunked scan; the agent reran the scan in two halves but with a one-word filter, and the three matters stayed unseen.

other_errors.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
other_errors.why: The listing at [61]-[62] showed one matter's default-judgment motion and damages affidavit, but it read only the petition and cited only that, so the proof-document criterion for that matter failed.
other_errors.critic_note: Review [71] questioned exclusions and unopened siblings but not the unread filings of a matter it included.

other_errors.why: The answer excludes two matters whose pleadings it had read at [26]-[48] (one as a specialty matter, one as defence-side), though both seek damages as the rubric expects.
other_errors.critic_note: Review [94] asked to reconcile the count and decide whether one excluded matter qualifies; the agent finished without acting.

other_errors.why: The answer lists an arbitration counterclaim matter as qualifying general commercial litigation although it is outside the qualifying set.
other_errors.critic_note: No review named that matter's inclusion.

runs.failure_point: One qualifying matter surfaced repeatedly but was never opened; it excluded another from its file listing alone, later edited out a third as defence-only, cited a letter instead of a pleading for a fourth, and added a non-qualifying matter.

first_error.why: The matter list at [38] (and later [56] and [62]) included a qualifying matter, but the nineteen matters it chose to list, and every later read, left it out, so it is absent from the answer.
first_error.critic_note: Review [50] flagged that only a subset of surfaced matters was listed; the agent reopened the stage and widened its scan, but never opened that matter.

other_errors.why: The answer excludes one matter as an employment dispute, judged from its file listing at [47]-[48] without reading its complaint.
other_errors.critic_note: Review [96] flagged exclusions not backed by reading documents; the check stages did not reopen it.

other_errors.why: For one included matter the answer grounds the demand in a pre-conference letter read at [78] instead of a pleading, so the proof-document criterion fails.
other_errors.critic_note: Review [90] flagged the letter read in place of the operative pleading and asked to open it; the agent wrote without doing so.

other_errors.why: The answer lists an arbitration counterclaim matter as qualifying although it is outside the qualifying set.
other_errors.critic_note: Review [96] flagged possible over-inclusion and asked to confirm every listed matter; the check stages removed two other matters instead.

other_errors.why: An edit removes a matter whose counterclaim seeks damages, calling it defence-only on a strict reading of the request.
other_errors.critic_note: Review [110] questioned the defence-only removals; attempt 2 only added an exclusion note.

divergence: All three runs failed, each in a different way after the same opening (capped listing, folder listing, a store-wide scan that timed out). T0's fallback file-name search hit its own line cap and its later scans filtered on one damages word, so three matters never surfaced (search miss at the file-name search; the critic flagged the cap and the agent's fix stayed too narrow). T1 and T2 surfaced every qualifying matter with file-name searches but chose subsets to open: T1 left three unread at its single big screening stage (critic flagged unopened candidates generically, ignored), T2 left one out at its candidate listing (critic flagged, the reopened stage did not reach it). All three runs then excluded matters they had read on narrow category judgements and asserted the same non-qualifying arbitration matter; reviews flagged some exclusions late and the agents finished without acting.
